page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton ARM64 processors. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz with a dedicated allocation of one thread per core. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

For high-speed local data access, the instance is bundled with 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. The combination of high-density ARM64 compute cores and massive local solid-state storage provides a highly resource-dense profile for workloads requiring rapid local I/O alongside high parallel processing capacity.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the custom ARM64 architecture delivers high compute density and power efficiency relative to traditional x86 architectures, lowering the resource-to-cost ratio for highly parallelized workloads. The instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads that also require high-capacity, low-latency local storage, such as distributed databases, large-scale data analytics, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based server powered by AWS Graviton processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and vCPUs operating at 3.3 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance is bundled with 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and supports a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. Designed without a GPU, this server leverages its high core count and massive local storage capacity to deliver efficient parallel processing. Qualitatively, the custom ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and cost efficiency for scale-out workloads. It is highly suited for distributed databases, data analytics, containerized applications, and compute-heavy workloads requiring rapid local storage I/O.
